correctness.rationale: The all-n asymptotic and concentration for fixed labeled q >= 4 are correct. First letter and bigrams give the unigram counts by adding the initial occurrence to incoming bigram counts. On a distinct-letter run chain the unique nonloop path forces every loop to be exhausted before leaving its vertex. There are q! binom(n-1,q-1) such words for n >= q. The type bound used in the proof is also valid: disjoint nonempty cyclic-root letter sets leave at most q long runs; at equality every root is a one-letter power, and the no-outside-occurrence property excludes any remaining letters outside those runs. Types with s < q contribute O_q(n^(q-2)) by the weighted one-equation count and bounded number of types, with the runless case supported at bounded lengths. Independently, for a singleton's Euler walk fix its last-exit tree to the terminal letter. Every vertex's departures other than its fixed tree exit (all departures at the terminal) must go to one common destination: otherwise permuting them gives a second trail, since a stopped incomplete walk would leave balanced unused edges whose last-exit tree leads to the already exhausted terminal vertex. After fixing this finite type, differences of free multiplicities must be circulations on a partial functional digraph, hence constant on each directed cycle and zero off the cycles; fixing total length removes one cycle parameter. The only q-cycle possibility uses all q self-loops, leaving a single path of tree exits, again the run-chain case. This is an infinite proof check, not an inference from finite enumeration.
residual_risks: No inference on growing q or subleading coefficients; no external attestation or formal verification.

evidence: Exactly q disjoint nonempty subsets of q letters exhaust the alphabet with single-letter roots. Such maximal types have empty connectors and each run of length at least three. Removing the requirement that runs have length at least three changes the number of chains by O_q(n^(q-2)); all shorter types cost at most the same order.

originality.rationale: The leading coefficient and concentration are not merely consistent with the prior upper bound; they follow directly from the stronger published finite-type structure and per-type counting rule. At k=2, q disjoint nonempty cyclic-root factor sets on q letters must be the q singletons. The cited exclusion of outside occurrences leaves exactly long monochromatic chains at maximal type; all other types are bounded by one lower power using the prior equation (8). Finishing with a count of permutations and positive compositions (and the elementary path argument for short runs) requires no new structural result. This is verified prior implication, not a claim that a prior paper printed the same q>=4 formula verbatim.
residual_risks: No claim of bibliographic exhaustiveness or an earlier verbatim formula. The known implication already suffices; restricted access to the DLT paper does not determine the verdict.
